about.title: About Me
about.subtitle: Who I am & what I do
description: My background in computer science has allowed me to work across software development, data analysis and research. I became particularly interested in understanding data, testing assumptions and explaining why a result occurs.

During my MSc in Computer Science and Engineering at DTU, I worked with machine learning, process mining, social data analysis and computational data science. My master's thesis took this further through a large-scale research project covering document processing, classification, manual validation and statistical evaluation.

I am now building my career in Data Analysis, with a focus on research data analysis and applied machine learning. My software development background helps me approach analytical problems with a structured, implementation-focused mindset.

thesis.title: Detecting Generative AI Declarations in DTU Master's Theses
thesis.description: Built an end-to-end Python document analytics workflow to identify and validate explicit Generative AI declarations across DTU master's theses.
bullets: Processed 943 analysable theses and 935 candidate passages
Combined PDF extraction, cleaning, regex rules, context windows and ambiguity guards
Manually validated evidence and compared rule-based results with an LLM classifier
Evaluated classification using agreement analysis, confusion matrices and statistical tests

worldHappiness.title: World Happiness Report - Predictive Modelling
worldHappiness.description: Prepared structured data for supervised learning and compared Logistic Regression with K-Nearest Neighbours using rigorous model evaluation.
bullets: Applied nested cross-validation for model selection and performance estimation
Used McNemar testing to compare model predictions
Visualized model performance and interpreted error patterns

hoursly.title: Hoursly: Time Tracking & Budgeting Web App

bullets: Secure user authentication and session management

Custom notifications with sound and visual alerts

processMining.title: Apollo Mission Process Analysis
processMining.description: Analysed NASA Apollo 1-17 mission event data across five mission phases using process mining and the Process Mining Project Methodology (PM²).
bullets: Prepared mission data and represented activities as event logs
Mapped recurring mission flows and compared execution paths
Investigated timing variation, exceptional paths and operational deviations

bullets: Evaluated FIDO2, TOTP, SMS-based 2FA protocols
Analyzed phishing detection mechanisms
Research paper and presentation delivery
